_doc: Character Level gives Stat Points. Job Level (separate EXP) gives Job Points for the Job Tree. Skill/Mod levels are raised with materials + gold. Respec costs in-game gold only.

character._statWheelDoc: Owner, 2026-10-29 (docs/STATS-TH.md): the six stats sit on a wheel in this order (VIT next to STR). A weapon asks for its type's stat (sword, greatblade, axe, mace STR; bow DEX; staff, wand INT; shields VIT), or a main and secondary pair (items.json secondaryStat; daggers are always a pair, STR/DEX or DEX/AGI; staves and wands never ask for VIT, a priest's VIT comes from an INT/VIT mace or a VIT/INT shield); a skill asks for one stat or two neighbours on the wheel (main first), a mod for one. Every stat named must be met on its own: none stands in for another. Stats come from trained points, Job Tree nodes and gear options (core/character.js statTotals).
character._lukDoc: LUK (owner, 2026-10-25): crit chance, a lucky dodge (dodgeChancePct: a monster hit misses entirely, capped at caps.dodgeChancePct; damage over time is never dodged; rolled on its own RNG stream, core/game-simulation.js damagePlayer) and a small drop find.
character._critOverflowDoc: Crit chance past 100% (no cap, owner 2026-10-25) turns into crit damage: each point over adds critOverflowToMultPct to critMultPct, outside the critMultPct soft cap and cap (core/character.js derive).
character._farmDoc: goldFindPct/materialFindPct/gearFindPct (Ranger farming line, hunter arrows) raise gold, material chances and gear drop chances on kills, up to caps; they add nothing to the power score.

respec._doc: Town only. Gold only: no rare items, no real money.

movementUpgrade._doc: Movement skill ranks (owner, 2026-10-25) are raised at the same workbench or trainer and with the same skill crystals and gold as a combat skill. Each rank above the first shortens the recharge by rechargePerLevel and lengthens the move by distancePerLevel (core/skills.js movementSkill). The skill's upgradeStat (a main stat: DEX for dash and roll, INT for blink, STR for leap; docs/STATS-TH.md) must reach the step's requiresStat.

skillGrowth._doc: Skill bars (owner, 2026-10-27/28, docs/SKILL-GROWTH-TH.md): each skill of a growth type has that type's bars (2 or 3). Bar points come from proficiency: casting a skill with an enemy within combatRange adds its own pace (the longer of its cooldown, cast time and 0.35 s), and every secondsPerPoint of that earns one point, up to totalPoints. A grade (C..S) caps how many points one bar takes (grades) and how many points the skill holds in all (gradeTotals: owner, 2026-10-29, so a long-used skill is not strong at its first grade); at that total proficiency stays full and waits for the next grade; it is raised at a workbench or trainer with gold, the skill's own gradeMaterial and a boss part. Each bar gains on one thing (gains add up) and pays on others (costs multiply); a cost on a stat the skill has no bar for is paid in MP at missingCostToMana of its strength. Speed (rate) joins the skill's haste under the central cap. count adds one projectile every countEvery points, fanned countSpread degrees apart, each projectile dealing (1/n)^countDamageExp of the hit. Taking points out (respec) costs respec.gold + respec.goldPerLevel x level per point; putting them in is free. core/skill-growth.js.

skillUpgrade._doc: Skill level (owner, 2026-10-27/29, docs/SKILL-GROWTH-TH.md): a skill levels from 1 up to the character's level (and maxLevel). Crystals fed to it at a workbench or trainer (including town.skillUpgradeStations) give skill EXP (crystals: EXP per crystal), and every EXP fed costs goldPerExp gold. Level L needs expPerLevel[0] + expPerLevel[1] x L EXP, rounded. Each level asks for stats (owner, 2026-10-29, docs/STATS-TH.md; core/skills.js skillRequires): the skill's requires (or require.base of its upgradeStat) plus require.perLevel per level above 1, shared by its stats in proportion; feeding reaches only levels the stats meet, and a skill above what the stats allow works at the highest level they meet. Feeding stops where the next level is out of reach (the character's level or the stat), so crystals are never wasted. perLevel/manaPerLevel: damage and MP cost per level above 1 (MP grows faster). Mod sockets follow the level (mods.slotLevels). Mods remain the source of behaviour changes. No failure or destruction.

modUpgrade._doc: Each rank above the first raises the mod stat requirement by requiresStatPerLevel (core/skills.js modRequires); an upgrade is refused until the next rank can be met.

openWorldSimulation._doc: Idle monsters sleep outside this conservative visible-area envelope. Combat/aggro actors remain active across every authored region; rendering may enlarge the pure-rule simulationRadius for an unusually wide view.

start._doc: New characters learn only the normal attack from their selected weapon. Other combat and movement skills are acquired later from quests or crafting.

opening._doc: Wake beside the wreck and choose one weapon. Only its normal attack is learned. No combat or movement skill selection. Firebolt and Ward remain quest/workbench rewards.

combat._doc: defenseConstant: armour takes defense / (defense + defenseConstant) of a hit (core/character.js defenseFactor; it grows with the raw numbers: 2026-10-25 every raw HP/attack/defense/damage/MP value was multiplied by 10). reflectFlat: the flat part of a guard reflect. Combat feel. Consecutive melee swings within comboWindow seconds alternate the arm side (animation only; every swing is the same strike, no finisher). Non-boss monsters flinch (stop moving) for stagger seconds when hit, but a started wind-up is never cancelled; a plain hit flinches a monster at most once per flinchLock seconds (owner, 2026-10-28: rapid light hits must not hold it in place), while a heavy hit's own stagger always applies.
combat._inputBufferDoc: A skill pressed while its cooldown has at most inputBuffer seconds left is remembered and cast the moment the cooldown ends (one press, the latest wins; not for charged or channelled skills), so a press a little early never feels dropped. core/game-simulation.js castSlot.

block._doc: A shield block lets through only `taken` of a hit from within arcDeg in front of the hero. Ground hazards and hits from behind are never blocked.

spellShield._doc: Spell shield (owner, 2026-10-25): a white pool over HP. Damage that gets through armour, block and a skill barrier takes the shield first, then HP (poison ticks too). It never heals; after rechargeDelay seconds without taking damage it refills rechargePctPerSecond of its maximum each second. Max = maxShield (INT, gear) x (1 + maxShieldPct). core/game-simulation.js damagePlayer / tick.

power._doc: Power score = sqrt(offence x defence) x scale (core/power.js). offence = sustained damage per second of the best slotted damage skill; defence = effective HP against a frontal hit. minOffence keeps a support-only loadout from reading 0.

balance._doc: Balance model (core/balance.js, tests/core/balance-model.test.js): a reference hero per kit fights the average normal monster of its level wearing the expected gear tier. Targets are what the tuning must keep. weaponFactor follows items.handRules (sword kit dual-wields two light weapons).

targets._doc: ttk: seconds to kill a same-level normal monster (the first levels are quick on purpose); ttd: seconds a hero survives standing in its hits without dodging; hoursToCap: playtime to the monster cap fighting same-level monsters (quests add more).

budgets._doc: Content budgets (owner, 2026-10-27; core/content-budget.js, tests/core/content-budget.test.js): a skill's score is what it adds to a reference hero of its weapon (budget score of rules.budgetWeights: log ratio per axis, team absolute); a main attack is scored against its weapon's reference main. A score outside its class band fails the test unless the item is in known, which lists today's items awaiting a decision with the reason; fixing one means removing it from known. support: buffs, heals, barriers, curses, summons, walls and counters (their party value is only partly measured, so the band is wide). mod: the best score a mod reaches on a skill it fits.

rules._doc: Build balance rules (owner, 2026-10-27; core/build-rules.js, tests/core/build-rules.test.js). A build is a kit, Job Tree nodes, a gear set and support skills; its profile has one number per axis (higher is better): single (boss DPS over fightSeconds, MP counted), pack (DPS into a pack of pack.size monsters within pack.radius m, from the main skill's shape), survival (seconds standing in the reference monster's hits, healing counted), sustain (seconds of the rotation before MP runs dry, up to fightSeconds), mobility (m/s of walking plus the movement skill), team (help per second the support skills give), income (gold-equivalent per hour). Standing out in a build's role is intended; overpowered means a build at equal cost dominates a build of another role (at least (1 - tolerance) of it on every axis and better by tolerance on one), or has no weakness (no axis below weakness x the field's best). Dominance within one role only marks the loser as a poor choice. Builds of one role compare on its axis within sameRoleGap. budgetWeights/budgetBand: a plan's weighted profile (each axis as a share of the field's best) may sit at most budgetBand above or below the median plan (too much or too little for the same points). recover: seconds a cooldown skill holds the hero after its cast (the rotation model fills the rest with the main attack). gearSets: the option ids a player stacks for that aim, spread over every slot (optionsPerItem each, mid rolls); a damage option a skill cannot use is skipped. growthSingleCap: no allocation of a skill's bars may lift its single-target damage past this share of the unspent skill, and none may be better at single, pack and MP at once (tests/core/skill-growth.test.js).

control._doc: Assumptions the profile uses for things it cannot see directly (check them in play): slowShare, how much of a slow keeps a monster from hitting (a chill only slows walking); tauntShare, how much of the pack a taunting summon draws; dodgeUse, how often a dodge is used against its recharge (on-dodge triggers); monsterSpeed, average walking m/s (knockback); burn/poison, the share of a hit a burn (15% x 3 s) or poison (12% x 4 s) adds; cap, the most control can take away; teamShare, how much of our control counts as help for the team; fanSingleShare, how much of each projectile past the first in a fan reaches one lone target (the rest fly past it; a pack takes one projectile per monster).

farming._doc: A Ranger who takes the whole farming line and shoots hunter arrows must out-earn a same-level sword hero after paying for the arrows, but the arrows must cost a noticeable share (tests/core/balance-model.test.js).
